title: Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the virtues of firm resolve, self-control, and wisdom
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the virtues of firm resolve, self-control, and wisdom Posted On:
                02 JUN 2026 8:30AM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today shared a Sanskrit Subhashitam, observing that firm resolve and self-control are the powers that make even the most difficult paths easy. Shri Modi highlighted that today, our youth are continuously engaged in nation-building with this very resolve. The Prime Minister posted on X: "दृढ़ निश्चय और आत्म-संयम वह शक्ति है, जो कठिन से कठिन राह को भी आसान बना देती है। आज हमारे युवा साथी इसी संकल्प के साथ राष्ट्र निर्माण में निरंतर जुटे हुए हैं। निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः। अबन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते॥" A person who begins a task after careful deliberation and with firm resolve, who never leaves it unfinished, who uses time wisely and who maintains complete control over their senses, such a person alone is truly wise. दृढ़ निश्चय और आत्म-संयम वह शक्ति है, जो कठिन से कठिन राह को भी आसान बना देती है। आज हमारे युवा साथी इसी संकल्प के साथ राष्ट्र निर्माण में निरंतर जुटे हुए हैं। निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः। अबन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते॥ pic.twitter.com/OboLRs7j9b — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) June 2, 2026 *** MJPS/SS/PRK (Release ID: 2267754) Visitor Counter : 937 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी , Assamese , Manipuri , Gujarati , Kannada , Malayalam Prime Minister's Office Prime Minister shares a Sanskrit Subhashitam highlighting the virtues of firm resolve, self-control, and wisdom Posted On:

title: Prime Minister greets the people of Telangana on Statehood Day
content:

title: Governor of Odisha interacts with Gujarat student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Governor of Odisha interacts with Gujarat student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI Gujarat student delegation explores Odisha’s cultural, educational and developmental landscape Posted On:
                02 JUN 2026 12:28PM by PIB Delhi The Governor of Odisha, Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, interacted with the Gujarat student delegation participating in Yuva Sangam Phase VI on 27th May 2026. The student delegation, led by the Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Ahmedabad, commenced its educational and cultural exchange visit to Odisha on 22nd May 2026. Hosted by the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Rourkela, the student delegation received a warm welcome on 25th May 2026, marking the beginning of an immersive learning and cultural exchange journey across the State. During the interaction, the Governor highlighted the role of youth in nation-building, cultural understanding, and strengthening the spirit of national integration. The session provided participants with valuable insights into leadership, civic responsibility, and the importance of fostering unity through cultural exchange. During their visit, the student delegation explored Odisha’s rich cultural, educational, and developmental landscape. Participants visited iconic sites such as the Konark Sun Temple and Maa Samaleswari Temple, gaining insights into the State’s spiritual and cultural heritage. They also experienced Odisha’s vibrant textile traditions through interactions with local artisans and engaged with the Munda tribal community through cultural exchanges and traditional performances. The student delegation participated in a session organised by the Central Institute of Indian Languages, which highlighted India’s linguistic diversity and its role in fostering cultural understanding. They also visited the National Institute of Technology Rourkela FTBI Lab, the Rourkela Steel Plant, Hirakud Dam, and Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium, gaining insights into Odisha’s innovation ecosystem, industrial development, engineering excellence, and sports infrastructure. As part of the sustainability-focused activities, the student delegation  joined the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ campaign, planting saplings and learning about environmental stewardship and organic farming practices. The visit concluded with a valedictory programme on 30th May 2026, marking the culmination of a meaningful journey of learning, cultural exchange, and national integration under Yuva Sangam. ***** AK (Release ID: 2267824) Visitor Counter : 52 Ministry of Education Governor of Odisha interacts with Gujarat student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI Gujarat student delegation explores Odisha’s cultural, educational and developmental landscape Posted On:

title: Governor of Telangana interacts with Meghalaya student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Governor of Telangana interacts with Meghalaya student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI Posted On:
                02 JUN 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi The Governor of Telangana, Shiv Pratap Shukla, interacted with the Meghalaya student delegation at Lok Bhavan, Hyderabad, on 28th May 2026. The student delegation, led by the Indian Institute of Management Shillong, is visiting Telangana as part of an educational and cultural exchange programme aimed at fostering national integration and cross-cultural learning among youth. Earlier, on 25th May 2026, the student  delegation received a warm welcome at the National Institute of Technology Warangal, the host institution for their visit to Telangana, marking the beginning of their immersive learning and cultural exchange journey across the State. During the interaction, the Governor highlighted the important role of youth in strengthening national integration, promoting cultural understanding, and contributing towards nation-building. The delegates shared their experiences from the Yuva Sangam journey and presented the Governor with a memento as a token of respect and remembrance. The interaction further enriched the participants’ understanding of India’s diversity, democratic values, and spirit of unity. The student delegation visited prominent cultural, educational, and innovation centres across Telangana, including iconic landmarks such as Hussain Sagar Lake, the Statue of Equality, Ramappa Temple, Warangal Fort, Bhadrakali Temple, and the Thousand Pillar Temple, gaining valuable insights into the State’s rich heritage, cultural legacy, academic excellence, and developmental initiatives. Participants also visited Kanha Shanti Vanam and T-Hub, where they were introduced to holistic well-being practices and India’s growing innovation and startup ecosystem. At NIT Warangal, they explored research and innovation facilities, participated in a plantation drive promoting environmental sustainability, and attended the valedictory programme on 30 May 2026, marking the culmination of their learning experiences and cultural exchanges during the Yuva Sangam journey. The student delegation departed for Meghalaya on 31st May, 2026. Launched by the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Yuva Sangam Phase VI seeks to strengthen national unity, cultural harmony, and emotional integration through immersive educational and cultural exchanges. The initiative brings together participants from 22 paired States and Union Territories, creating pathways for a deeper understanding of India’s diversity, innovation ecosystems, and shared aspirations for nation-building. ***** AK (Release ID: 2267817) Visitor Counter : 59 Ministry of Education Governor of Telangana interacts with Meghalaya student delegation under Yuva Sangam Phase VI Posted On:

title: Shri Manohar Lal reviews Power Sector issues in the State of Haryana
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Power Shri Manohar Lal reviews Power Sector issues in the State of Haryana Haryana to commence smart metering works from 31st August Posted On:
                02 JUN 2026 11:12AM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, reviewed the matters relating to the power sector for the State of Haryana at Chandigarh yesterday. The meeting was attended by Shri Anil Vij, Minister for Power, Government of Haryana, along with senior officials from the State Government, Ministry of Power, Government of India, and Power Sector CPSEs. The meeting started with the Shri Manohar Lal highlighting the key areas where the State Power department and the State Power sector PSUs could work on with a detailed action plan. Matters relating to the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) and operational and financial parameters of the DISCOMs were discussed. The Union Minister emphasised that electricity is an economic good and that the utilities must be operated on sound commercial principles, with a focus on reducing the cost of power purchase, rationalising expenses, and augmenting revenue. He noted that while AT&C losses had improved consistently over the years, however, it should be ensured that the performance improves further. He highlighted the need for timely settlement of Government department dues and subsidies through an automated payment mechanism. He reviewed the progress of smart metering and advised expeditious award of works. The State committed to start smart metering works on ground from 31 st August. He further emphasised the need for phased rollout of prepaid smart metering, beginning with Government consumers and employees, followed by high-end consumers with load more than 10kW, with appropriate incentive mechanisms for voluntary conversion. Shri Manohar Lal advised the State to undertake all loss reduction works on priority with time-bound completion targets. He also reviewed the status of resource adequacy and intra-State Transmission planning, and advised the State to resolve outstanding issues and ensure that capacity addition keeps pace with demand growth. Progress under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana was also reviewed and the State was directed to prepare a focussed action plan for expanding consumer enrolment under the scheme. This will help reduce the power costs of these consumers. Shri Manohar Lal noted that sincere efforts will go a long way in making the State DISCOMs financially viable and the State power sector self-sufficient. He assured the State of Government of India’s continued support and cooperation for the overall development of the State. Shri Anil Vij, Minister for Power, Government of Haryana, assured that the State shall take all necessary measures for implementation of the sanctioned works and improving the overall performance of the State’s power sector. *** NR/MD (Release ID: 2267784) Visitor Counter : 338 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Power Shri Manohar Lal reviews Power Sector issues in the State of Haryana Haryana to commence smart metering works from 31st August Posted On:

title: NHRC takes suo motu cognizance of 53 maternal deaths within a year due to lack of facilities in the Sidhi District of Madhya Pradesh
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau National Human Rights Commission NHRC takes suo motu cognizance of 53 maternal deaths within a year due to lack of facilities in the Sidhi District of Madhya Pradesh Reportedly, the district has consistently ranked among the bottom three districts in the Community Maternal Health League grading conducted by the State Health Department Issues notice to the Madhya Pradesh Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks Posted On:
                02 JUN 2026 11:21AM by PIB Delhi The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report about the deaths of 53 expecting mothers during pre and post-delivery in the Sidhi district of Madhya Pradesh in one year between April 2025 and March 2026 primarily due to lack of awareness and medical facilities. Reportedly, the Sidhi district has consistently ranked among the bottom three districts in the Community Maternal Health League grading conducted by the State Health Department. The Commission has observed that the contents of the media report, if true, raise a serious issue of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, seeking a detailed report within two weeks. According to the media report, carried on 29 th May 2026, out of the 53 maternal deaths, the average age of the deceased has been reported to be 26 years, with most of them first or second-time mothers. The news report has also revealed a lack of basic infrastructure, including doctors and technical experts at Community Health Centres, Primary Health Centres and the District Hospital, due to which patients are referred to higher medical facilities in the faraway Rewa District, risking life in transit. Reportedly, an ambulance driver disclosed that several villages do not have proper road connectivity in Sidhi District, complicating matters further during the monsoon season. The pregnant women have to be carried on cots for two to three kilometres before reaching an ambulance. *** NSK (Release ID: 2267786) Visitor Counter : 375 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी National Human Rights Commission NHRC takes suo motu cognizance of 53 maternal deaths within a year due to lack of facilities in the Sidhi District of Madhya Pradesh Reportedly, the district has consistently ranked among the bottom three districts in the Community Maternal Health League grading conducted by the State Health Department Issues notice to the Madhya Pradesh Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks Posted On:
